questions.q: What is the difference between == and is?
questions.a: == checks value equality; is checks object identity. Prefer is None for None checks.

questions.q: Explain LEGB with one practical bug.
questions.a: Local -> Enclosing -> Global -> Built-in. A nested function may read an outer name; accidental globals can make tests/order unpredictable.

questions.q: Why are mutable default arguments risky?
questions.a: The same default object is reused across calls. Use None, then create the list/dict inside the function.
A generator yields values lazily and uses less memory for large streams; a list stores all values eagerly.
The outer container is copied but nested mutable objects can still be shared.

questions.q: How do you debug an unexpected TypeError?
questions.a: Reproduce, inspect values/types, isolate the smallest failing expression, change one thing, rerun and add a regression test.
loc uses labels; iloc uses integer positions.
A one-to-many or many-to-many join increases row count. Validate key uniqueness/cardinality before aggregating.
axis=0 reduces across rows and typically keeps column-wise results; axis=1 reduces across columns and keeps row-wise results.

questions.q: Why is shape important in NumPy?
questions.a: Shape determines broadcasting compatibility and matrix multiplication dimensions.
WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.
INNER keeps matched rows; LEFT keeps all left rows and fills unmatched right columns with NULL.
It computes analytics across related rows without collapsing them, e.g. rank, running sum or lag.

A simple baseline gives a reference point and prevents complicated models from appearing useful without evidence.
Precision asks how many predicted positives were correct; recall asks how many actual positives were found.
It converts text into model-readable token IDs/subwords.
Longer sequences increase memory/latency; truncation can also remove useful information.
Retrieve relevant external context and pass it to the generator so answers can be grounded in that retrieved information.
RAG adds external context at inference and is useful for changing knowledge; fine-tuning changes model behavior/weights for a task or style.
A workflow follows predefined steps; an agent can choose among actions based on state/model decisions, but reliable systems still bound tools and steps.

questions.q: How do you stop an agent loop?
questions.a: Max steps, timeouts, explicit stop conditions, tool errors and fallback states.

questions.q: What belongs in a production API answer?
questions.a: Contract, validation, status codes, timeouts, auth, secrets, logging, observability and failure handling.
Provider/network failures otherwise keep resources occupied and increase tail latency.

questions.q: Explain your AI chatbot in 60 seconds.
questions.a: Problem -> Flask/REST entry -> NLP/intent routing -> response generation -> MySQL/SQLite history -> frontend -> one failure case -> next improvement.
It provided a lightweight Python web layer with clear routing and easy REST integration; the service layer remained modular.
For NLP-based query processing/intent recognition and routing. Explain the exact components you actually implemented.
Webhook -> validation -> AI decision -> allowed tool/API/DB action -> condition/error path -> audit/approval where needed.

questions.q: How would you defend the 60% reduction claim?
questions.a: State the baseline, measurement period, activities counted and calculation. Use the number only if you can reproduce the measurement.

questions.q: What if you do not know an answer?
questions.a: Say what you know, state the assumption, reason from principles and avoid inventing details.

questions.q: What is your coding interview process?
questions.a: Clarify inputs/outputs/constraints -> examples -> simplest correct approach -> code -> complexity -> tests -> edge cases.
Hash map for complement lookup; average O(n) time and O(n) space.
For contiguous subarray/substring problems where window state can be updated incrementally.
Sorted or monotonic search space and a condition that lets you discard half the search space.

questions.q: How would you design a resilient LLM endpoint?
questions.a: Validate input -> bounded provider call -> timeout/retry policy -> structured output validation -> logging/metrics -> safe error response.
Only needed context: current task, validated inputs, tool results, step count and decision metadata; avoid unnecessary long-term personal data.

questions.q: Where should human approval be added?
questions.a: Before irreversible/high-impact side effects when automated mistakes would be costly.

questions.q: What do you monitor in an AI app?
questions.a: Quality/task success, latency, provider errors, cost/token usage, retries, tool correctness and safety/invalid actions.

questions.q: Which project should you explain first?
questions.a: Pick the project most relevant to the interviewer question, then explain the architecture and your specific contribution.
